name: Gearbox
text: Add Elements to Video as a skill to EXCAVA’s toolkit. This lets us insert new visual elements into existing footage without rebuilding scenes from scratch, saving time and preserving the high-quality source material we already have. The trade-off is that some elements may not blend perfectly with the original lighting or perspective, but the speed gain outweighs minor visual inconsistencies for most use cases.

name: Torque
text: The real risk isn’t blending—it’s that adding elements to video demands pixel-perfect masks, lighting matches, and motion tracking that most tools botch. Instead, pre-process footage with a tool like Runway’s Gen-4 for consistent style and depth, then layer elements in a controlled pipeline; settle the argument by running a blind test comparing the original vs. the modified clip for artifacts.

name: Gearbox
text:
Use Runway Gen-4 to pre-process EXCAVA’s footage first. It stabilizes lighting, depth, and style across shots, making later element insertion cleaner and faster—this is the highest-leverage step to raise quality without rebuilding scenes. The trade-off is extra compute time upfront, but it cuts rework downstream and preserves source integrity better than patching flaws later.

name: Torque
text: Runway Gen-4’s upfront compute cost isn’t the real risk—it’s that forcing a single style across diverse footage will erase EXCAVA’s unique visual signature, turning high-quality source material into a generic look. Instead, pre-process only the shots where lighting or motion breaks element insertion, then use a lightweight diffusion model like FLUX-dev for targeted fixes; settle the argument by running a blind A/B test on 10 diverse clips—if Gen-4’s style uniformity scores lower than targeted fixes, we scrap the global pre-process and adopt the surgical approach.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Pre-process only problematic shots in EXCAVA’s footage with Runway Gen-4 for lighting/depth fixes before element insertion—Torque owns the pipeline and validates output against EXCAVA’s visual signature.
